analysis.headline: US G60 is winning on core BMW driving character, but customers are tripping over the digital operating concept, seat comfort/adjustability, and EV-use practicality.
analysis.summary: In the US, the G60’s strongest asset is still the thing customers expect from a 5 Series: it drives very well. Handling/Maneuverability scores 6.058 and Overall driving performance 6.039 in the US study, with 210 likes for Handling / Riding and 349 likes for Drivetrain. Customers repeatedly praise smoothness, road holding and acceleration. The main product risk is that this strength is being diluted by usability friction. Infotainment & Digital Services is the largest complaint domain with 752 complaints and 70% complaint share, and the study’s Menu structure of infotainment system is a weak 4.879. Customers describe the car as feature-rich but too complex, too menu-heavy and too dependent on touch interaction. Seats are another priority issue: 62 complaints, level-A finding, with repeated reports of discomfort, hard-to-find settings and insufficient adjustment. For BEV/PHEV users, EV range confidence and charging practicality are also material pain points: Electric Range has 67 complaints and Public charging / external providers 55. Practicality details matter too, especially the unreliable hands-free trunk opening and broader storage/console frustrations already reflected in findings and requirements. Overall, the product manager should protect the driving/ride character, while first simplifying high-frequency interactions and removing comfort/practicality irritants that customers face every day.
analysis.data_coverage: Analysis uses the US context pack plus drilled-down evidence from verbatims for Seats, Operating concept, Electric Range, non-contact trunk lid opening, Handling / Riding and Drivetrain; US study metrics for climate controls, infotainment menu structure, handling and driving performance; US sales; equipment checks for wireless charging and comfort seats; and the full set of derived US requirements. Evidence depth is strong for the main issues: 3,628 verbatims in scope for US market voice, with large complaint counts in infotainment, seats, EV range and trunk access. Findings cited as level A/B indicate stronger support, but verbatim sources are unweighted and Source B mixes product and process notes.

insights.title: Driving dynamics are the core strength and should be protected
insights.statement: The G60 is strongly validated in the US on its core driving brief. Handling / Riding has 210 likes, Drivetrain has 349 likes, and the study scores are very strong at 6.058 for Handling/Maneuverability and 6.039 for Overall driving performance. Verbatims consistently praise smooth ride, road holding and immediate acceleration.

insights.title: The operating concept is too complex for frequent in-drive tasks
insights.statement: Infotainment & Digital Services is the largest complaint domain with 752 complaints and a 70% complaint share of classified rows. Within it, Operating concept, operating system has 53 complaints, including 39 Difficult to Use rows, and the study attribute Menu structure of infotainment system is weak at 4.879. Customers repeatedly say functions are buried in menus, touch interaction is distracting while driving, and the system feels less intuitive than prior BMWs or other vehicles they know.
insights.customer_quote: Really like the vehicle overall, but the user interface should be more straightforward.

insights.title: Seat comfort and adjustment are a daily-use pain point
insights.statement: Seats are a major recurring complaint with 62 complaint rows and a level-A finding. The drilled verbatims show two linked problems: baseline comfort and adjustment usability. Customers report lower-back pain, overly firm seats, insufficient height/tilt range, and confusion because some adjustments are split between seat controls and touchscreen menus. Comfort seats are optional in the catalogue rather than standard across variants.
insights.customer_quote: the driver seat is extremely uncomfortable, especially in the lower back area

insights.title: Climate-control usability reinforces the broader HMI problem
insights.statement: Climate interaction is not just a minor annoyance; it is one of the weakest measured attributes in the US study at 4.804 for Operation of heater/ AC controls. This aligns with the existing level-A finding for Air conditioning, setting and supports the broader pattern that common comfort functions are not direct enough to access or manage.

insights.title: EV customers question both real-world range and range transparency
insights.statement: Electric Range is a substantial complaint theme with 67 complaints, 50 of them Difficult to Use. The issue is not only absolute range but confidence in the displayed estimate, especially in cold weather. Customers describe unexpectedly low miles after charging, large drops over routine trips, and erratic or insufficiently transparent range information. This sits alongside 55 complaints on public charging / external providers, showing that EV-use friction is both in-car and ecosystem-facing.
insights.customer_quote: EV range display feels erratic, the number jumps around after each trip

insights.title: Hands-free trunk access is unreliable enough to damage everyday practicality perception
insights.statement: Space & Practicality has a very high 78% complaint share, and non-contact trunk lid opening alone has 44 complaints, mostly usability-related. Customers say the kick gesture is inconsistent, hard to learn, sometimes works only after repeated attempts, and in some cases opens unintentionally. This is a small feature in isolation, but it is a frequent daily-use irritant and stands out because some customers compare it unfavorably with prior BMWs.
insights.customer_quote: It rarely works on the first try and sometimes will not work at all even after several attempts.

insights.title: The product is feature-rich, but complexity is eroding perceived quality
insights.statement: Body equipment, overall technology appears as both a strength and a complaint theme: 201 likes but also 98 complaints. Customers appreciate the amount of technology, yet many describe the car as something they have to 'figure out'. This suggests the issue is not lack of features but the cognitive load of learning and controlling them. That matters because it can undermine the premium impression even when the hardware and feature content are strong.
insights.customer_quote: there are so many features that it becomes confusing

insights.title: US volume is large enough that fixing these issues has meaningful impact
insights.statement: The US is a major G60 market with 75,600 units in 2024 and 78,000 in 2025, with an 80,000 plan for 2030. Given this scale, improvements to high-frequency usability and comfort issues would affect a large installed base and future volume.

recommendations.title: Simplify access to the most-used driving and comfort functions
recommendations.proposal: Consider a near-term HMI simplification focused on one-touch access for climate, seat heating, steering-wheel heating, drive mode, assistance on/off, map and phone, with less menu depth while driving and stronger shortcut persistence per profile.
recommendations.rationale: This is the clearest cross-cutting pain point: the largest complaint domain, a level-A operating-concept finding, and a weak study score for infotainment menu structure. Customers are not asking for fewer features; they are asking for faster, more intuitive access to the features they use most often.

recommendations.title: Rework seat comfort tuning and make adjustment easier to understand
recommendations.proposal: Consider improving front-seat comfort calibration and adjustment usability within the current generation, especially lumbar flattening, height/tilt range, and clearer separation or guidance between physical seat controls and touchscreen-only adjustments.
recommendations.rationale: Seats are a level-A complaint with repeated reports of pain, firmness and awkward adjustment. This is a daily-contact issue that can overshadow the otherwise strong driving experience.

recommendations.title: Make climate control more direct and persistent
recommendations.proposal: Consider giving climate functions more direct access and ensuring key settings persist reliably by driver profile, while also reviewing cooling performance for hot-soak conditions relevant to US use.
recommendations.rationale: Climate controls are one of the weakest measured attributes and already have a dedicated level-A finding and requirement. This is a practical subset of the broader HMI issue and likely one of the fastest ways to reduce frustration in daily use.

recommendations.title: Improve EV range transparency before promising more hardware change
recommendations.proposal: Consider first improving customer-facing range confidence through better estimation logic, clearer condition-based range communication, and more transparent explanation of temperature and usage effects; then assess whether a larger hardware/range step belongs to the successor plan.
recommendations.rationale: The evidence shows two problems: customers want more range, but they also distrust the displayed range and do not understand how conditions affect it. Better transparency and estimation are more achievable in H1 than a major battery-system change.

recommendations.title: Stabilize hands-free trunk operation or reduce false-trigger behavior
recommendations.proposal: Consider a focused fix for the kick-to-open trunk function so activation is more consistent, easier to learn and less prone to unintended opening, especially for digital-key users.
recommendations.rationale: The complaint count is high for a single convenience feature, and the issue is repeated in very similar terms across sources. Because it is a frequent real-world interaction, even a narrow fix could noticeably improve practicality perception.

recommendations.title: Protect the current ride and handling balance in future updates
recommendations.proposal: Consider treating the current ride/handling character as a protected attribute in both lifecycle changes and successor planning, avoiding fixes in other areas that compromise steering precision, ride composure or acceleration feel.
recommendations.rationale: This is the strongest and most consistent positive in the US evidence. It is the reason many customers forgive other issues, so it should be preserved while usability and comfort are improved around it.

assumptions_and_gaps: Country-level verbatims are effectively US-only here (3,610 US, 18 CA), but study metrics, sales and findings are market-level US data by definition.

The equipment catalogue is the German July 2026 list; it shows what the model line offers, not US standard/optional content. Equipment references are therefore used as offer/context evidence, not as proof of US packaging.
No direct study metric for EV range was retrieved in this drill-down, so the EV assessment rests mainly on verbatim volume and findings rather than a study-score gap.
The requirements result was truncated in the tool output, but the relevant cited requirement ids and texts for the main recommendations were visible and used.
Source B contains call-centre notes and can mix product feedback with process content; repeated patterns across multiple sources were prioritized for conclusions.
BMW Group document search returned broad corporate passages rather than a precise US-market strategy statement, so document evidence was not needed for the core product conclusions.
